prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

BAGHDAD, Iraq (CNN)  -- Coalition forces found 26 bodies buried in mass graves and a bloodstained "torture complex," with chains hanging from walls and ceilings and a bed connected to an electrical system, the military said Wednesday. Twenty-six bodies were found in mass graves near a "torture complex" discovered by coalition forces. The troops made the discovery while conducting an operation north of Muqdadiya, Iraq. From December 8 to 11, the troops who found the complex also killed 24 people they said were terrorists and detained 37 suspects, according to a statement issued by Multinational Division North at Camp Speicher in Tikrit. The moves were part of an operation called Iron Reaper that has been in progress across northern Iraq for the past few weeks. The complex was in an area thought to be an al Qaeda in Iraq haven and operating base, the military said. Iraqis had told the military about the site during an earlier operation. "Evidence of murder, torture and intimidation against local villagers was found throughout the area," the military statement said. Ground forces first found what appeared to be a detention facility, which was one of three connected to the torture complex, Multinational Division North said. One of the facilities appeared to have been a headquarters building and a torture facility, it added. As the area was cleared, the bodies were found. Eventually, 26 bodies were uncovered in mass graves next to what were thought to be execution sites, the military said. The bodies are believed to have been dead between six and eight months, according to a gruesome military video shot at the scene. Some had their hands tied behind their backs. Identification is proving to be a challenge because of advanced decomposition. Photos given to the news media show a filthy bed wired to an electrical system, with an outlet hanging from wires on the wall. In the video, troops point out rubber hoses and boxing gloves, a ski mask and a blood-covered sword and knives. Other still photos show an entrance to the underground bunker and barbed wire stretched outside it. A short distance away from the complex, troops found a bullet-riddled Iraqi police vehicle. Some of the bodies may belong to Iraqi police, according to the military video. The operation netted nine weapons caches, which have been destroyed, the military said. They included anti-aircraft weapons, sniper rifles, more than 65 machine guns and pistols, 50 grenades and a surface-to-air missile launcher and platform, the statement said. Also found were mines, pipe bombs, rocket-propelled grenades, mortar tubes and rounds and 130 pounds of homemade explosives. E-mail to a friend .

outputs.L1:
**BAGHDAD, Iraq (CNN) —** Coalition forces discovered 26 bodies buried in mass graves near a bloodstained “torture complex” equipped with chains hanging from the walls and ceilings and a bed connected to an electrical system, the military said Wednesday.

Troops made the discovery during an operation north of Muqdadiya, Iraq. Between December 8 and 11, the forces that found the complex also killed 24 people they identified as terrorists and detained 37 suspects, according to a statement issued by Multinational Division North at Camp Speicher in Tikrit.

The actions were part of Operation Iron Reaper, which has been underway across northern Iraq for the past several weeks. The complex was located in an area believed to be an al Qaeda in Iraq haven and operating base, the military said. Iraqis had alerted the military to the site during an earlier operation.

“Evidence of murder, torture and intimidation against local villagers was found throughout the area,” the military statement said.

Ground forces initially discovered what appeared to be a detention facility—one of three sites connected to the torture complex—Multinational Division North said. Another facility appeared to have served as both a headquarters and a torture center.

As troops cleared the area, they began uncovering bodies. Ultimately, 26 bodies were found in mass graves beside what were believed to be execution sites, the military said.

According to a graphic military video recorded at the scene, the victims were believed to have been dead for six to eight months. Some had their hands tied behind their backs. Advanced decomposition has made identification difficult.

Photographs provided to the news media show a filthy bed wired to an electrical system, with an outlet suspended from wires on the wall. In the video, troops identify rubber hoses, boxing gloves, a ski mask, and blood-covered swords and knives. Other still photographs show the entrance to an underground bunker and barbed wire stretched outside it.

A short distance from the complex, troops found a bullet-riddled Iraqi police vehicle. According to the military video, some of the bodies may be those of Iraqi police officers.

The operation also yielded nine weapons caches, all of which have been destroyed, the military said. The caches contained anti-aircraft weapons, sniper rifles, more than 65 machine guns and pistols, 50 grenades, and a surface-to-air missile launcher and platform, according to the statement.

Troops also found mines, pipe bombs, rocket-propelled grenades, mortar tubes and rounds, and 130 pounds of homemade explosives.

*E-mail to a friend.*
outputs.L2:
BAGHDAD, Iraq (CNN) — The U.S.-led coalition discovered 26 bodies in mass graves near a blood-spattered site described as a “torture complex,” the military announced Wednesday. Chains were suspended from the walls and ceilings, and a dirty bed had been wired to an electrical system.

The site was uncovered during an operation north of Muqdadiya, Iraq. Between December 8 and 11, the troops involved also killed 24 people whom the military identified as terrorists and took 37 suspects into custody, Multinational Division North said in a statement issued at Camp Speicher in Tikrit.

The action formed part of Iron Reaper, an operation that had been under way across northern Iraq for several weeks. According to the military, the complex was located in an area believed to serve as both a refuge and operational base for al Qaeda in Iraq. Iraqi residents had alerted coalition forces to the location during an earlier mission.

The military statement said signs of killings, torture and threats against nearby villagers were present throughout the site.

Ground troops initially encountered what seemed to be a detention center, one of three facilities linked to the complex, Multinational Division North said. Another structure apparently functioned as both a headquarters and a place where torture was carried out.

As forces secured the area, they began finding human remains. Ultimately, 26 bodies were exhumed from mass graves beside locations believed to have been used for executions. A graphic military video recorded at the scene indicated that the victims had likely been dead for six to eight months. Several had their hands bound behind them. Because the remains were severely decomposed, identifying the victims has been difficult.

Photographs supplied to news organizations show a grimy bed connected to electrical wiring, with an outlet dangling from wires along a wall. In the military footage, soldiers identify rubber hoses, boxing gloves, a ski mask, and bloodstained knives and a sword. Additional images depict the entrance to an underground bunker and barbed wire installed outside.

Not far from the complex, troops located an Iraqi police vehicle covered with bullet holes. The military video suggested that some of the dead could have been Iraqi police officers.

Forces also seized nine weapons stockpiles, all of which were destroyed, the military said. The caches contained anti-aircraft arms, sniper rifles, more than 65 pistols and machine guns, 50 grenades, and a surface-to-air missile launcher with its platform. Mines, pipe bombs, rocket-propelled grenades, mortar tubes and ammunition, and 130 pounds of homemade explosives were also recovered.

Coalition forces taking part in Operation Iron Reaper near Muqdadiya, Iraq, discovered what military officials described as a suspected al Qaeda torture and execution complex, along with nearby mass graves. The site was located after local Iraqis alerted troops and provided information about violence carried out against villagers in the area.

During a search of the complex and surrounding ground, troops recovered the remains of 26 people in various stages of decomposition. Some of the victims had been bound, and evidence at the scene suggested that captives had been tortured before being killed. The condition and placement of the bodies indicated that the location had been used repeatedly rather than for a single incident.

Military officials said the discovery illustrated the systematic methods used by insurgents to terrorize local communities, punish suspected opponents, and discourage residents from cooperating with Iraqi or coalition forces. Information from villagers was crucial to finding the site, underscoring the growing willingness of some Iraqis to report insurgent activity despite the threat of retaliation. The remains were turned over to the appropriate Iraqi authorities for identification and further investigation.

- **Several torture facilities and execution sites**, including rooms with bloodstained walls and floors, chains or restraints, electrical wiring used for shocks, and other implements of torture.
- **Victims and human remains:** troops freed or located abused detainees and found graves or dumping sites containing **about two dozen bodies**, including civilians. Some victims reportedly showed signs of torture and execution.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a detailed CNN-style report on the discovery of 26 decomposed bodies, alleged execution sites, torture equipment, and weapons during a coalition operation near Muqdadiya.
counterfactuals.output:
**Coalition forces discover 26 bodies, suspected torture sites near Muqdadiya**

**MUQDADIYA, Iraq** — Coalition troops operating near the volatile city of Muqdadiya discovered the decomposed remains of 26 people, along with suspected execution sites, torture equipment and caches of weapons, according to a coalition statement.

The remains were found during an operation in the predominantly rural area surrounding Muqdadiya, northeast of Baghdad in Diyala province. The region has been contested by insurgent groups, militias and Iraqi security forces and has experienced repeated sectarian violence.

Coalition officials said troops searching several locations uncovered what appeared to be sites used to detain, torture and kill captives. Equipment allegedly associated with torture was found inside or near the compounds, along with weapons and other material believed to have belonged to militants.

The condition of the bodies suggested the victims had been dead for some time. Officials did not immediately identify them or say precisely when or how they were killed. Forensic examinations would be needed to determine the victims’ identities, causes of death and whether all 26 were connected to the same group or period of violence.

The coalition described some of the locations as apparent execution sites, but independent journalists and investigators were not immediately able to verify that assessment. It also remained unclear who controlled the compounds before the operation or which armed faction may have been responsible for the deaths.

Weapons recovered during the searches included firearms, ammunition and other military matériel, according to the coalition. Officials did not provide a complete inventory or say whether the weapons could be directly linked to the bodies or alleged torture facilities.

No immediate statement was available from Iraqi authorities on plans to secure the remains, conduct autopsies or notify victims’ families. Coalition officials said the evidence would be turned over for further investigation.

Muqdadiya and the surrounding Diyala River Valley have long been strategically important because they connect Baghdad with routes leading north and east toward the Iranian border. The area’s mixed Sunni and Shiite population has also made it a flashpoint for insurgent attacks, militia activity, kidnappings and retaliatory killings.

The discovery underscores the difficulty of determining responsibility for clandestine detention and mass killings in areas where several armed groups have operated. Human rights organizations have repeatedly called for alleged mass graves and torture sites in Iraq to be protected, documented and examined by qualified forensic teams.

Authorities had not announced any arrests directly linked to the 26 deaths. The victims’ identities and the circumstances surrounding their killings remained under investigation.
